title: Pointer + length
theory:
### Pointer-length pairs by hand

Higher-level languages expose **slices** as pointer, length, and sometimes capacity.
In assembly you implement that trio yourself: one register holds the **base address**,
another holds the **element count** or **byte length**, and you advance the base when
you trim the front.

Negative lengths are meaningless; treat lengths as unsigned quantities and guard loops
so **`rcx`** does not wrap from zero with **`loop`** unless you intend the full **2⁶⁴**
iteration degenerate case—which you almost never do.

### Walking a range

A common idiom compares a running pointer to an end pointer computed as **`base + length`**
or decrements an explicit counter. Choose the pattern that keeps the fewest registers
live across **`syscall`** boundaries.

```nasm
; rsi points at first byte, rdx is byte length (already matches write syscall args)
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    syscall
```

### Re-slice without copying

Trimming prefix bytes only adjusts **RSI** and **RDX** for **`sys_write`**: the backing
storage stays put in **`.data`** or **`.bss`**. That mirrors how string views and byte
slices share storage in managed languages—only here there is no borrow checker to catch
use-after-trims gone wrong.

exercises.title: Middle window
exercises.description: Buffer `db '0','1','2','3','4'` lives in `.data`. Set `rsi` to address of `'2'` and `rdx` to `3`; issue one `write` to print `234` (no newline), then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db '0','1','2','3','4'
section .text
_start:
    ; lea rsi ... buf+2 ; mov rdx, 3 ; write
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db '0', '1', '2', '3', '4'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel buf+2]
    mov rdx, 3
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Empty slice
exercises.description: Call `write` with `rdx=0` (zero-length) and any valid `rsi` (use `buf` label). Should print nothing; exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db 'X'
section .text
_start:
    ; write(fd=1, buf, 0)
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db 'X'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel buf]
    mov rdx, 0
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Pass slice to helper
exercises.description: Write `emit` that expects pointer in `rdi` and length in `rsi`, performs `write` to stdout, returns. `_start` passes `buf` and length `4` for bytes `abcd`.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db 'a','b','c','d'
section .text
emit:
    ret
_start:
    lea rdi, [rel buf]
    mov rsi, 4
    call emit
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: Inside `emit`, `mov rax,1; mov r8,rdi; mov r9,rsi; mov rdi,1; mov rsi,r8; mov rdx,r9; syscall`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd'
section .text
emit:
    mov rax, 1
    mov r8, rdi
    mov r9, rsi
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, r8
    mov rdx, r9
    syscall
    ret
_start:
    lea rdi, [rel buf]
    mov rsi, 4
    call emit
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Prefix window
exercises.description: Buffer `db 'p','q','r','s'` in `.data`. One `write` with `rsi` at the start and `rdx=2` must print `pq` (no newline), then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db 'p','q','r','s'
section .text
_start:
    ; rsi = buf, rdx = 2
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: Prefix slice: pointer is `buf`, length is `2`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    buf: db 'p', 'q', 'r', 's'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel buf]
    mov rdx, 2
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
